ashby:demandbase:67ada533-3bd1-4127-94ed.summary:
Demandbase is the only pipeline AI platform that empowers GTM teams to automate growth at scale. With a unified view of data, insights, actions, and outcomes, B2B enterprises can seamlessly align and execute their account-based GTM strategies with confidence. Thousands of businesses trust Demandbase to maximize revenue, minimize waste, and consolidate their data and tech stacks – all in one platform.

As a company, we’re as committed to growing careers as we are to building world-class technology. We invest heavily in people, our culture, and the community around us. We have also continuously been recognized as One of The Best Places To Work in the San Francisco Bay Area by Fortune, and One of The 60 Best Companies To Sell For by Selling Power. Our offices are located in San Francisco, New York, Austin, Seattle, India, and the United Kingdom.

sections.title: The Role
paras: With the rise of LLMs, and the prevalence of ML-models to find patterns in customer data, we’re noticing the B2B SaaS space move from being able to generate meaningful insights based on data to being able to execute meaningful actions against the insights generated.

At Demandbase, we believe our Orchestration Engine (the system that allows B2B teams to automate their Go-To-Market strategy at scale) is core to our value proposition. As the Lead Product Manager for Orchestration , you will be the primary architect of this "Action Layer."

You will lead a high-impact team focused on building the logic, triggers, and workflows that connect our rich account intelligence to real-world execution. Your challenge is twofold: maintaining a world-class, high-scale orchestration platform while strategically infusing Demandbase AI to move toward more intelligent, agentic use cases.

sections.title: Strategic Responsibilities
bullets: Drive the Orchestration Roadmap: Own the end-to-end lifecycle of our workflow builder, trigger logic, and action framework. You will ensure our orchestration engine is the most flexible, reliable, and user-friendly tool in the B2B market.

Deepen the Integration Fabric: Drive the strategy for how our engine interacts with the broader tech stack (Salesforce, Marketo, Slack, etc.). You’ll ensure that complex, multi-step "Plays" execute seamlessly across distributed third-party ecosystems.

Pragmatic AI Integration: Instead of "AI for AI's sake," you will identify specific orchestration friction points—such as manual segment building or rigid workflow rules—and solve them using Demandbase AI .

Bridge to Agentic Use Cases: Lay the groundwork for autonomous GTM. You will define how our orchestration logic can support emerging Model Context Protocol (MCP) standards, allowing AI agents to "understand" and "trigger" existing workflows safely.

ashby:matter-labs:a7b55498-adf4-43d4-a1b.summary:
Matter Labs builds private settlement infrastructure that lets regulated institutions settle directly with each other without exposing data, ceding control, or waiting days. Global finance moves $4 quadrillion a year on systems designed for paper and telex. The institutions that built them - from clearing houses to exchanges to the world's largest banks, institutions are now actively replacing them. We're building what comes next.

Our core product, Prividium, gives each institution its own private settlement environment (a Prividium Zone) with independent governance and built-in interoperability across counterparties, asset classes, and jurisdictions. Settlement happens through zero-knowledge proofs: one party proves a transaction is valid without revealing any underlying data to the counterparty. The only private settlement infrastructure built on zero-knowledge cryptography.

ashby:relayfi:cc637f37-94a5-4d04-888d-f6.summary:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

At Relay, product management is about outcomes, not outputs. We start with real customer problems and build solutions that move the needle for SMBs, and for our business. Our team pairs long-term vision with rapid iteration. We believe that trust is a product feature, and that usability, reliability, and polish aren't afterthoughts, they're core to how we earn the confidence of business owners.

sections.title: Why this role matters
paras: Signing up for a business bank account is the easy part. The hard part is the distance between "account opened" and "this is where I run my business." That distance is where most SMBs quietly stall; the first deposit that never lands, the payroll still running out of the old account, the bookkeeper who was never invited in. Every business owner who doesn't cross it stays on the cashflow tightrope we exist to get them off of.

As Senior Product Manager, Growth (Activation), you own that crossing. You'll own the journey from first login to funded, transacting, habitual use of Relay — and the systems, experiments, and in-product moments that get customers there faster and in greater numbers. This is a metrics-owning role: you'll be accountable for activation rate, time-to-first-deposit, and depth of product adoption in the first 90 days, and for the revenue those unlock.

sections.title: In your first year, you might:
bullets: Rebuild the post-signup experience so a new owner reaches their first funded transaction in days, not weeks
Diagnose where and why customers drop between account approval, funding, and first payment, then ship the sequenced interventions that close those gaps
Stand up the experimentation and lifecycle infrastructure that lets Relay run activation tests continuously rather than one-off
Drive adoption of the products that make Relay sticky (multiple accounts, cards, bill pay, accounting integrations) by getting them in front of the right owner at the right moment
Partner with Risk and Operations so that friction we add for good reasons (KYC, fraud controls) costs us as few good customers as possible
Build the narrative and roadmap that aligns leadership, Marketing, and CX around a shared definition of an activated customer

sections.title: What you'll be doing:
bullets: Own activation end-to-end: define the vision, set the roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements to how quickly and completely SMBs start running their money through Relay
Treat activation like a business: define the activation metric that actually predicts retention and revenue, instrument it, monitor it, and make decisions rooted in data and customer insight
Run a real experiment engine: form hypotheses, design tests, read results honestly, and kill what doesn't work, while knowing when a problem calls for a rebuild rather than an A/B test

Ship high-quality product from ideation to launch: partner closely with design and engineering as part of a leadership trifecta, raising the bar for usability, craft, and polish. Onboarding copy and empty states are your job, not someone else's
Work across the whole first-run surface: in-product experiences, lifecycle messaging, and the handoffs between Marketing, Sales, and CX that make or break a new customer's first month
Stay deeply connected to SMB customers: watch real owners set up their accounts, understand what makes them hesitate to move their money, and design for the trust that earns

Champion product culture at Relay: bring curiosity, ownership, and a high bar for quality that elevates the product team as a whole

sections.title: Як саме проходить робота?
bullets: Будуєш довгострокові відносини з власною базою преміум-користувачів - вони знають тебе на ім’я та звертаються саме до тебе;
Супроводжуєш користувача під ключ: вирішуєш щоденні запити, складні кейси та працюєш із ситуаціями, коли користувач планує залишити продукт;
Самостійно ведеш комунікацію через email, онлайн-чати та дзвінки й відповідаєш за якість досвіду зі своєю базою користувачів;
Працюєш з AI та автоматизаціями, які забирають рутинні задачі та дозволяють фокусуватися на комунікації й пошуку найкращих рішень;
Стаєш голосом користувача всередині команди: помічаєш інсайти, передаєш їх продукту та безпосередньо впливаєш на покращення користувацького досвіду.

sections.title: У SKELAR ми побудували середовище для професійної самореалізації:

Так команди бізнесів фокусуються на продукті — а 10+ команд в складі Platform закривають функції Legal, Finance, HR, Admin, Talent Acquisition, Employer Branding, IT та інші.

— Нетворк та обмін досвідом як частина культури. Серед наших колег — кофаундери, які запустили не один бізнес, а також найсильніші спеціалісти на ринку. Тож ми маємо доступ до необхідної експертизи на відстані витягнутої руки.

ashby:socure:4aba09cb-32f2-4a45-8815-885.summary:
Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. sections.title: Why Socure?
paras: As a Senior Pre-Sales Solution Consultant, Gaming you will be the primary technical point-of-contact throughout the sales cycle for online gaming, sports betting, fantasy sports, and predictions prospects in the Gaming & Predictions pod. You will be responsible for understanding client requirements, designing end-to-end onboarding and transaction risk workflows, and demonstrating how Socure’s platform delivers measurable impact across conversion, fraud losses, bonus abuse/arb, and operational efficiency.

You will collaborate closely with Sales, Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to run high-impact discovery, architect solutions, and lead proof-of-concepts that de-risk technical decisions and accelerate deal cycles. You will also serve as a bridge between technical and non-technical stakeholders, ensuring that complex model performance, data flows, and integration patterns are communicated clearly to executives, product leaders, and risk/compliance teams at our customers.

sections.title: Job Responsibilities
bullets: Serve as the day-to-day technical expert for igaming, sportsbook, fantasy sports, and predictions opportunities, partnering with Account Executive Directors as the primary pre-sales Solution Consultant for your territory and segment.

Design end-to-end identity and fraud workflows across Socure’s products including API integration patterns, decisioning logic, rules, and data orchestration, with a focus on gaming-specific use cases such as multi-accounting, bonus abuse, self-exclusion, and responsible gaming controls.

Collaborate with Data Science to scope, design, and execute proof-of-concepts (POCs) and backtests for gaming and sportsbook prospects, defining success metrics, evaluation methodology, and governance; interpret results and present clear recommendations to both technical and executive stakeholders.

Participate in business development activities including building and delivering compelling demos, presenting solution recommendations, contributing to RFPs/RFIs, and helping construct statements of work (SOWs) and pricing scenarios that align technical scope with commercial structure.

Act as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders (CRO, CISO, CTO, Head of Risk/Compliance, VP of Product, Head of Player Protection) by simplifying complex statistical and technical concepts—such as model performance, threshold strategies, swap sets, and regulatory implications—into actionable business decisions.

Partner with post-sales Solution Consultants, Customer Success, and Technical Project Managers to ensure smooth handoffs from pre- to post-sales, including documenting solution assumptions, success criteria, and implementation risks to protect value realization and retention.

Stay ahead of gaming and the prediction market industry trends, fraud and identity attack vectors, and evolving regulations impacting digital onboarding, payments, geolocation, and responsible gaming; use this knowledge to guide clients and influence internal strategy.

sections.title: Job Requirements
bullets: 7+ years of professional experience, including at least 4+ years in a client-facing technical role such as solution consulting, sales engineering, professional services, or technical pre-sales within enterprise SaaS, data products, or risk/identity platforms.

Meaningful experience in online gaming, sportsbook, fantasy sports, or adjacent regulated digital wagering/payments environments—ideally with exposure to digital onboarding, age and identity verification, KYC/KYB, transaction monitoring, or fraud/risk management workflows.

Demonstrated track record leading complex, multi-stakeholder pre-sales engagements end-to-end: discovery, solution design, demo strategy, POC/backtest design, success metrics definition, and technical close support.

Strong technical depth across modern SaaS and data architectures, including RESTful APIs, event-driven or batch data integrations, rules/decision engines, analytics, and familiarity with ML/DS-adjacent technologies.

Ability to synthesize complex statistical and technical information—such as model performance, lift curves, ROC/AUC, threshold optimization, or swap sets—into clear, business-oriented recommendations for risk, product, and executive stakeholders.

Experience acting as a bridge between technical and non-technical audiences, with excellent written and verbal communication skills and a strong executive presence; comfortable presenting to C-level and board-level stakeholders at high-growth gaming operators and digital wagering companies.

Proven collaboration skills across Sales, Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success, with the ability to influence without authority and drive alignment in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.

Demonstrated commitment to Socure-aligned leadership behaviors: continuous learning and improvement, effective and transparent communication, ownership and accountability for outcomes, mentoring and uplifting teammates, sound judgment under uncertainty, and adaptability through change.

sections.title: ABOUT SPRUCE
paras: Our mission is to let users control their data across the web. We build privacy-preserving, standards-based digital identity and credentialing systems that help governments and institutions increase access to important services and benefits programs while reducing fraud. We believe the right approach to product management is critical to combining high standards of usability, security, and privacy into a seamless user experience and driving broad adoption.

sections.title: THE ROLE
paras: We are seeking a Forward Deployed Product Manager to sit alongside our government customers during discovery, architecture, and design, sometimes while engineering is building, and help them work out what they actually need and why.

You will support specific deployments, from statewide identity programs to large-scale education and workforce credentialing initiatives. Each must be localized to its own ecosystem: stakeholders, user demographics, regulations, and program objectives. Even as we sell a product to a customer, we treat the overall program as a product with its own governance, roadmap, and objectives. Much of this work is customer-driven today and requires hands-on engagement with individual implementations, even as we work to consolidate what we learn into reusable Spruce products. Holding both at once is the job.

A credential is only useful if someone issues it, someone accepts it, and someone carries it. So beyond discovery, you own adoption for your program: getting issuers to issue, verifiers to verify, and end users to adopt, with startup-style resourcefulness and measurable KPIs. In some cases, you will source and build the first pilot group yourself.

sections.title: 1. CUSTOMER-EMBEDDED DISCOVERY
bullets: Work directly with state government partners through discovery, architecture, and design
Understand their users, policy environment, constraints, and workflows first-hand
Look past stated requirements to the underlying problem the customer is actually trying to solve
Navigate government relationships thoughtfully: introduce user evidence that may challenge stated priorities, and influence direction without damaging the relationship

sections.title: 2. END-TO-END PRODUCT OWNERSHIP
bullets: Hold the full product picture across user-facing experiences and the APIs and services beneath them, often across several interconnected initiatives at once
Help partners shape and sequence their roadmap, and make sure what gets built solves the real problem
Partner closely with engineering, design, and delivery leads from definition through deployment

sections.title: About the role
paras: Claude Science is an AI workbench that gives researchers a single environment for work that today spans dozens of disconnected tools — literature, specialized databases, scientific computing, analysis, and publication-ready outputs. Claude Science already renders protein structures, genome tracks, and chemical structures natively, and coordinates multi-agent workflows with built-in review for citation and calculation errors — and we're just getting started. Much of this is being built 0→1 right now, in a category no one has defined yet.

We're growing the Claude Science product team. As a Product Manager on Claude Science, you will own a major area of the roadmap end to end — think expanding into new scientific fields, landing new model capabilities with researchers, or making the workbench ready for enterprise R&D teams — and help shape the overall product direction alongside the rest of the team. You'll spend real time with researchers in academic labs, biotech and pharma R&D, and research institutes to understand how science actually gets done — from hypothesis to analysis to publication and beyond— and turn what you learn into shipped product. You'll partner directly with our research teams to make the models better at science, help decide which fields and workflows we go after next, and shape what it takes for Claude Science to be trusted in enterprise and regulated research environments.

We're looking for experienced product managers and founders with technical depth: people who can learn the unique needs of a structural biologist or a computational chemist, get in the weeds of model transcripts and evals, and still zoom out to help define a product category. We're open to deeply technical product experts who are excited to support scientific discovery; expertise in a scientific field is not required, but the ability to ramp in a new domain quickly is paramount.You thrive in ambiguity, uncover non-obvious use cases for nascent capabilities, and bring those insights back to research.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Anthropic sells Claude through partners as well as directly. In the public sector, those partners matter more than anywhere else. As Channel Partner Manager, Public Sector, you will own Anthropic's reseller and distributor relationships across US federal, state and local government, and you will build the operations that let those partners transact with us quickly and cleanly.

Your time will be split roughly evenly between two kinds of work. The first is partner management. You will be the primary Anthropic contact for our public sector partners, agree on a joint plan with each of them, and work with our public sector account teams so that partner and direct motions support each other rather than collide. The second is channel operations. You will onboard new partners, instance an agreement for each of them, run deal registration, administer rebates, and keep the program's processes and records in order.

Every partner adds a fixed amount of operational work regardless of revenue, so the processes you build will determine how quickly public sector customers can buy. Much of this does not exist at Anthropic yet, and building it to a standard our partners and teams can rely on will be a large part of your first year.

greenhouse:chainguard:4712509006.summary:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

sections.title: The role, in a nutshell:
paras: Chainguard secures the software supply chain, and we're standing up a new team to build a new product inside it.

Agents now write a large and growing share of the world's code, and they inherited a CI system designed for humans who push a few times a day. Write, push, wait in a queue, reinstall the same toolchain, scrape the logs, try again. Agents iterate far more often than people do, so they feel every minute of that, and the workarounds they've grown are worse than the thing they're working around. We don't think the fix is a faster version of the CI you already have. We think CI gets rebuilt for agents, and that's what we're doing.

The product isn't launched, so a job post is the wrong place for the details. What we can tell you now: the team is small, the hard technical pieces already run in production inside Chainguard, and you'd be driving the product direction.

sections.title: What you'll own:
bullets: Strategy and roadmap. Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the product. Decide what we build first, what comes next, and what we're not going to do.

0→1 product work. Take this from a system that works for us to a product customers buy and use. Bring structure to problems that don't have any yet, make the tradeoff calls, and get things in front of users before they feel finished.

How agents actually build software. Go deep on how developers and their agents write, test, review, and ship code today, including the parts nobody blogs about. Most of what's written about agentic development is aspirational. You'll work from what people really do.
Design partners. Find the teams whose agent fleets are big enough to hurt, get the product into their hands early, and turn what they tell you into priorities.
Developer experience. Adoption is the whole game here. Own how the product gets tried, configured, and lived with, so a team can move onto it without running a migration project.
Launch. Positioning, naming, docs, the pricing model, and the story, with Product Marketing and the rest of Product. You're also the person who says when it's ready.
Cross-functional leadership. Partner with Engineering, Experience, Product Marketing, and other Product leaders, and keep a small team pointed at the same thing while the space shifts underneath it.

sections.title: What we're looking for:
bullets: 5+ years of product management experience on developer-facing, infrastructure, security, or similarly technical products.

You've built agent tools. Something agents use, or something people use to build with agents: a coding agent, an agent framework or harness, MCP servers, eval systems, or developer tooling meant to be driven by a model instead of a person. This is the requirement that matters most to us.
You know CI from the inside. Builds, tests, caches, runners, artifacts, merge gates, and the specific reasons pipelines end up slow, flaky, and expensive. You should have opinions about why.
You don't need to be a GitHub Actions expert. We're not building a better Actions, and years of workflow YAML isn't the experience we're hiring for. Knowing where it breaks is.
Experience taking a technical product from an early idea through launch and iteration.
Judgment about what to leave out. A new product dies from doing too much as easily as from doing too little.
Comfort with a deeply technical engineering team. You can hold your own in a design discussion and disagree with an engineer about a tradeoff.
You talk to developers directly and often, and you can tell the difference between technology people find interesting and a product they'll actually adopt.

bullets: You've run coding agents in production at real volume, or built the systems that keep them from breaking things.
Experience with developer platforms, build systems, remote execution, or hosted development environments.
Experience with containers, Kubernetes, registries, or other cloud-native infrastructure.
You've built security products for developers, and you know how fast a developer abandons one that gets in the way.
Experience with products that serve individual developers and large enterprises at the same time.
You've owned your own team's CI at some point and hated it.

greenhouse:coalition:4724543005.summary:
Coalition is the world's first Active Insurance provider designed to help prevent digital risk before it strikes. Founded in 2017, Coalition combines comprehensive insurance coverage and innovative cybersecurity tools to help businesses manage and mitigate potential cyberattacks.

Opportunities to make an impact with bold thinking are real—and happening daily at Coalition.

sections.title: About the role
paras: This is a new role leading a new grouping of three areas that together form Coalition's risk lifecycle: Underwriting (how we select and price risk), Claims (how we close the loop and mitigate losses when something goes wrong), and Security (the Control and Wirespeed products that help policyholders reduce risk in the first place). Each of these has historically been run as its own domain. Your job is to be strategic about how these areas come closer together, recognizing that risk selection, loss mitigation, security telemetry, and claims outcomes are not separate problems but one continuous feedback loop.

This is a people-leadership role. You will manage a team of product managers across all three areas, help to steer the strategy that connects them, and be accountable for how the combined areas perform. You'll report into product leadership and partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Underwriting, Claims, Actuarial, Finance, Operations, and more.

Most of the value in Active Insurance comes from the connections between these functions, not the functions themselves. Security signals from Control and Wirespeed should sharpen how we underwrite. How a claim develops should feed back into how we price risk. The quality of underwriting should shape our loss exposure and therefore our claims load. Today these loops exist, but they aren't owned by anyone as a whole.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Ensure that our product strategy across underwriting, claims, and security is consistent and treats them as one risk lifecycle, and make the deliberate trade-offs about where to invest across the three.

Build and develop the product team beneath you, including hiring, coaching, and holding a group of PMs to a high standard across three distinct domains, each with its own stakeholders and technical depth.
Own the feedback loops between areas: ensure security telemetry informs underwriting, claims development informs pricing, and underwriting quality is measured against realized loss outcomes.

Partner with Data and Engineering to advance model-driven workflows, automated decisioning, and ML-assisted tooling responsibly while managing the operational and regulatory considerations that come with automated decisions in a regulated product.
Drive major platform evolution and systems migrations across the portfolio, in close partnership with your engineering counterparts.
Define success metrics that span the portfolio, not just each area in isolation, and use quantitative and qualitative data to prioritize and make trade-offs.
Represent these areas to executive leadership, brokers, and cross-functional partners, translating between deep technical work and business outcomes.
Use AI consistently in how you and your team work, and champion an AI-enabled approach to underwriting, claims, and security products.

greenhouse:counterparthealth:8345966.summary:
At Counterpart Health, we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant. By supporting Primary Care Physicians (PCPs), we deliver improved outcomes at lower cost through early diagnosis and longitudinal care management of chronic conditions.

We're hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the longitudinal patient record, one trusted view of the care each patient receives across every setting, from the primary care office to the specialist to a hospital stay. Every Counterpart product builds on this record.

Our clinical data comes from hundreds of sources, including health information exchanges, EHRs, labs, ADT feeds, pharmacy fills, prior authorizations, and claims from our health plan customers. Each one captures part of a patient's care. The longitudinal record connects them into one history of the patient's visits,…

sections.title: What you will own and improve
bullets: Product strategy. Set the vision and roadmap for the longitudinal record. Find the highest-value problems across the products and programs that depend on it, and make the trade-offs among completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and investment.

Data for every use case. The record serves providers at the point of care and the programs that depend on complete care history: quality measurement (HEDIS), risk adjustment and RADV audits, payment integrity, and revenue operations. Providers, quality analysts, and operational teams all work from the same care history.

How every source becomes part of the record. You own patient matching, deduplication, normalization, and clinical terminology mapping, which turn raw data from each source into a trusted part of the patient's record. Every new source runs through them, so improvements are built once and reused across products.

Adoption. A canonical field counts only when clinicians use it. You own the path from definition to adoption: requirements, a migration plan per use case, and retiring fragmented, duplicate versions of the same data.

sections.title: What success looks like
bullets: The record gets more complete, accurate, and timely, and you can show it with numbers.
Products and programs adopt the shared record and retire their own versions of it.
New customers and markets reach a usable patient record with less time and less one-off work.

You can show what those gains changed downstream: more complete evidence for quality and risk adjustment, earlier visibility into admissions and care transitions, and fewer inconsistencies across products.
You run a clear decision process with clinical and engineering partners, and definitions are documented, adopted, and applied consistently.

sections.title: You should get in touch if
paras: About Counterpart Health: In 2018, Clover Health set out to do something unprecedented: build a clinically intuitive, AI-enabled solution that fits within physicians' workflows to help support the earlier diagnosis and management of chronic conditions.

Years later, that vision is a reality, with thousands of practitioners using Counterpart Assistant during patient visits to improve disease management, reduce medical expenses, and drive success in value-based care.
With an exceptional team of value-based care and technology experts, Counterpart Health is driving value-based care at the speed of software.

sections.title: Come Build with Us
paras: We're a NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We're an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. We are now signing more programs than any one person can implement, which makes the capacity and quality of the implementation team the real constraint on how fast our mission travels. This role owns that.

Reporting to the Head of Implementation, you will lead and grow a team of Implementation Managers and Associates taking pharma and life sciences clients from kickoff through go-live and hypercare. paras: A team that owns outcomes. You will lead a team of Implementation Managers and Associates running high stakes launches for pharma and life sciences clients. Launches that land on time, across a portfolio. You'll track delivery KPIs including on-time launch rate, implementation CSAT, and project budget management, and make sure every launch hands off cleanly to the Engagement team. Risks surface early and get driven to resolution across internal and external teams. No surprises at go-live.

Deliverables that are client-ready before they leave the building. You'll review your team's discovery notes, solution designs, and project plans so that what reaches a client reflects Courier Health at its best, while building the platform and data-model judgment in your team that lets them get there without you over time.

sections.title: What Makes You Successful
bullets: 10+ years in customer-facing implementation, professional services, solutions delivery, or technical program management at a B2B SaaS company.
2+ years managing implementation, delivery, or professional services talent. You have given hard feedback and watched someone get better because of it.
A track record of personally owning complex, multi-phase enterprise implementations end to end, with multiple client stakeholders and parallel technical workstreams.

Optimize Environment Patching: Identify and resolve systemic environment blocks, reviewing infrastructure configurations to ensure streamlined, compliant patch deployment pipelines.

Maintain Guardrails & Compliance: Navigate and implement evolving operational frameworks within secure facilities (SCIF), ensuring all GovCloud interactions strictly meet rigorous federal security benchmarks.

Solid baseline familiarity with Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
Hands-on debugging and systems administration experience inside major public cloud boundaries (specifically AWS, Azure, or GCP platforms).
Strong foundation in Linux/Unix systems engineering, containers (Docker/Kubernetes orchestration mechanics), and automated patch deployment pipelines.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
Ability to work out of our McLean, VA secure facility, including flexibility to support 24x7 operational coverage frameworks within a SCIF environment as required.

Own the range-setting product and analytics roadmap end to end and carry launches to market — adoption, enablement, and change management.

paras: We're looking for an evidence-based, customer-centric, and inventive Staff Product Manager to build Parts into a product line and a revenue stream at Fleetio. Reporting to the Senior Director of Product Management for the Maintenance Division, you'll partner with a cross-functional team of engineering, design, data, and go-to-market, and work closely with our Maintenance Shop Network (MSN, our outsourced maintenance business unit), Payments, and in-house Maintenance teams. sections.title: About the Role:
paras: As Senior Product Manager for Commerce, you will own Taskrabbit's global commerce platform, which covers how clients pay for their tasks and how Taskers get paid for their work. The Commerce team's goals are to make it easy for clients around the world to book and pay, get Taskers their earnings quickly and reliably, reduce what we spend to process payments, and keep our payments platform compliant and reliable in every market we operate in. As the PM for the team, you will propose, shape, and execute the initiatives that move us toward these goals. You'll lead a team made up mainly of backend engineers and partner with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Support, Risk, and Legal to identify problems, prioritize the work that matters most, and deliver it.

We're looking for someone who knows the payments landscape well and can lead independently from day one. You don't need marketplace experience. What matters more is that you care about the people on both sides of a payment, you dig into problems until you understand why they happened, and you're comfortable going deep into how payments systems work behind the scenes.

sections.title: What You'll Work On:
bullets: Own the global commerce platform, including client payments (e.g., payment methods, booking experience) and Tasker money movement (e.g., payouts and earnings) across every market we operate in.

Improve how payments work for our users, e.g., launching new payment methods that increase booking conversion in different markets, reducing payout delays for Taskers, and removing friction from checkout.

Investigate payment issues end to end. When something goes wrong (a spike in declines, a delayed payout, numbers that don't match what Finance sees), you'll find the root cause using every tool available, including AI tools to explore data and system behavior.
Plan and sequence the team's initiatives with your engineering lead and drive them to delivery, balancing user-facing improvements, cost reduction, compliance requirements, and platform health.
Prioritize ruthlessly. There will always be more work than the team can take on, so you'll decide what moves the needle and be clear about what we won't do.
Partner closely with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Support, Risk, and Legal, and communicate the roadmap and outcomes to Taskrabbit senior leadership.

sections.title: Your Areas of Expertise:
bullets: Payments experience: You have deep experience building B2C payments products (e.g., integrating with payment processors, adding payment methods like PayPal, BNPL, or SEPA, managing payouts), and you know the landscape well enough to lead with minimal supervision from day one. Global payments experience is a strong plus.

Product sense for payments: You understand how the payment experience shapes user behavior and business outcomes, and you can tell which improvements will actually move conversion, retention, or cost. You track metrics like authorization and decline rates, and you know where to look when they move.

Prioritization: You have a strong sense of what moves the needle, and you make tradeoffs with conviction. You're comfortable saying no, explaining why, and keeping the team focused on the highest-impact work with limited resources.

Stakeholder relationships: You build trust with partners across the company, gather input from many sources, and turn it into a clear plan. You've worked with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Support, Risk, and Legal teams and understand what each of them needs from a payments platform.
Execution and communication: You get things done, remove blockers, and roll up your sleeves when needed. You communicate clearly in writing and in person.

paras: You thrive in challenging environments where innovation is key. Your passion for technology is matched only by your drive to redefine its limits. You seek more than a job; you seek a calling—a chance to make a lasting impact on the digital landscape.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're looking for a Digital Product Manager who can own a client engagement end-to-end — from scoping to shipped product — across three kinds of work: building new AI agents, standing up greenfield products the agentic way, and helping established companies rebuild aging platforms and level up their teams to work AI-natively. You'll sit between clients and agentic engineering teams, turning ambiguous business problems into scoped, sequenced, shippable work — whatever form that work takes.

This isn't a role for someone who's only managed roadmaps in a single-product SaaS company, and it isn't a narrow "AI agent PM" role either. Some engagements will be zero-to-one greenfield builds. Some will be rebuilding a client's legacy platform without breaking what already works. Some will involve teaching a client's own team how to build and ship AI-natively so they don't need us in the room forever. You've worked in an agency or consulting environment, you know how to run multiple client relationships at once, and you know how to say "no" to a client gracefully when the ask doesn't hold up.

sections.title: About Noble Machines
paras: Noble Machines builds general-purpose robots that take on the most dangerous and physically demanding jobs in heavy industry, so that doing that work becomes a choice, not a necessity. Our robots work in construction, mining and energy, where dust, heat, uneven ground and the unexpected are normal conditions, not edge cases.

We were founded in 2024 by engineers from Apple, SpaceX, NASA and Caltech. We came out of stealth in March 2026, after shipping robots to a Fortune Global 500 customer within 18 months of starting. We're a Series A team in Sunnyvale, and we're building the next generation of Moby, our general-purpose robot, now.

sections.title: About the role
paras: You'll be the product lead for what Moby can do and how it gets deployed. On one side, you'll work with our AI, software and hardware engineers to decide which skills and capabilities we build next, and how we test and validate them. On the other, you'll work with customers and our field team to make sure a robot arrives on a jobsite, gets set up quickly and does real work from week one.

This is a hands-on role on a small team. You'll set the roadmap and write the specs. You'll spend time on customer sites watching how work actually gets done, and bring what you learn back into requirements engineers can build against. You'll report to our CEO and work daily with engineering, field operations and the commercial team.
This role is a fit if you like being the person who connects a robot's lab performance to what happens on a muddy site at 6 a.m.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own the roadmap for robot capabilities and deployment tooling, from scoping and sequencing through release, and hold the sequence when priorities conflict.

Turn field reality into requirements. Visit customer sites, observe operators and supervisors, and translate site conditions and edge cases into clear requirements and measurable performance targets (for example, task success rate, cycle time, payload and terrain limits).
Write specs engineers build against without back-and-forth : product requirements, acceptance criteria and validation plans for new skills, autonomy features and operator interfaces.
Work across AI, software and hardware. Make trade-offs between what the robot learns, what the hardware can support and what the customer needs on site.

Build the deployment path. Define how a customer evaluates, pilots and rolls out a robot, from site assessment and setup through acceptance testing and handoff, and the internal tools that make it repeatable.
Partner with field operations on onboarding, operator training and site documentation, so adoption doesn't depend on any one person.
Define and track success metrics such as task success rate, interventions per hour, uptime, MTBF/MTTR and time from arrival to productive work, and use them to set priorities.
Represent the product with customers and prospects during evaluations, and feed what you hear back into the roadmap.

sections.title: What success looks like in your first six months
bullets: A written roadmap that engineering and leadership agree on, with sequenced milestones and explicit dependencies.
Engineering teams building and releasing against your specs, with agreed validation criteria for each release.
A field requirements guide that captures real site conditions, constraints and the edge cases that matter most.
At least one customer pilot or site deployment run on the onboarding and acceptance process you defined.
A small set of core metrics (task success, interventions, uptime, time-to-deploy) measured regularly and driving roadmap decisions.

bullets: Co-own the game's feature roadmap with Product, Game Design, Production and the external development studio. Drive prioritization of features that strengthen the meta experience and IP expression, support the LiveOps strategy, and maintain a healthy game economy.

Develop the LiveOps event framework and cadence strategy from scratch, defining event types, reward structures and seasonal beats — then execute and iterate a content calendar that maximizes engagement, retention and monetization.

Champion the IP in product decisions: ensure that events, offers, collections, and progression milestones express the brand in ways that resonate with the target audience. Partner with Game Design and the external studio to translate IP strength into product requirements and content strategies that drive engagement and monetization.

Define LiveOps requirements for the external development studio, review builds, provide feedback on design decisions that impact economy and progression, and ensure the publisher–studio feedback loop is tight and productive.

Keep a pulse on player sentiment via app reviews, community channels, and surveys. Translate feedback into testable hypotheses in coordination with Game Design to inform event design and economy tuning.
Work cross-functionally across Production, Game Design, Engineering, and Marketing to align on objectives and execute key beats.

sections.title: What We’re Looking For:
bullets: 4+ years of experience in free-to-play mobile games in a Product Management or LiveOps role.

Direct experience working on a casual mobile game with strong meta-layer or collection/customization systems such as fashion, lifestyle, or dress-up games strongly preferred (e.g. Covet Fashion, Design Home, or similar IP-driven titles). Match-3 or puzzle experience is a plus.

Deep understanding of F2P LiveOps mechanics, meta-progression systems, and game economy fundamentals — you've built or tuned event frameworks, collection or customization loops, and offer strategies, with a track record of measurable impact on engagement and revenue KPIs.
Strong experimentation instinct — you default to testing hypotheses and move fast to learn and iterate.
Experience using data tools (BigQuery, Excel/Sheets, Tableau or similar) to drive decisions, including working with economy models and sink/source analyses.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to present key learnings to the broader team.

sections.title: Additional Information
paras:
Base pay is one part of our total compensation package. Pay is established on an individual basis after considering multiple factors such as relevant experience, education, and other qualifications. Performance-based discretionary bonuses and variable pay plans are available for some positions. Work Environment
This job is available remotely. When not remote, this job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers and phones.

sections.title: Physical Demands
paras: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The employee is required to sit for prolonged periods of time; balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. The employee is required to operate essential office equipment, such as computer/laptop, phone, keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment on a regular basis.
